balanced.rule: Shor.Balanced.defaultRule: s = min width, L = max width; if s < 2 or L = s: unchanged; if 2L <= 3s: pad the small operand to L (one product at L x L); else B = ceil(L/s) blocks, B-1 low blocks of width s-1 zero-extended to t, top block L-(B-1)(s-1), all products at t = max s top, block i at angle phi*2^(i(s-1)); applied only if fitsB (existing reserves suffice), else the original site
balanced.widths: the equal-width core runs at the post-balance operand widths, so nextWidth (exact) is evaluated there

checks.axioms: #assert_axioms _root_.PolicySubmission.policy in Submission/PolicyCheck.lean: fails the build on native_decide (its compiled-evaluator axiom), sorry (sorryAx) or any declared axiom, so every band's side conditions really did go through the kernel
checks.correctness: Shor.policy_submission_correct: proved once, generic in the policy; no per-submission proof. Shor.submission_correct is the one-band case at threshold 0
checks.ir_agreement: Shor.Reflect.policySubmissionChecks (probe design): the document is well formed and its two dispatchers are exactly dispatcherTemplate of this policy (routing proved: Emit/Symbolic/Dispatcher.lean). The sampled checks run on the PROBE submission - the same band setups in the same order (so the same band bodies and coeff offsets) at the smallest strictly decreasing thresholds where each band's table shrinks (a band whose table never shrinks is probed at the leaf) - with the dispatchers rebuilt for it: each band body one level deep at its probe threshold (child calls as the compiler's phase-product leaves, width and capacity arguments checked against the registers passed) = the compiler's one-level step; full-depth instantiate = real compiled circuit at the probe ladder widths within the leaf budget, in both reserve regimes; odd qft widths straddling the lowest probe threshold; the leaves; and the reference Shor instances. Evaluated natively by this executable, which prints this document only if the check is true. Cost depends on the tables only, not on the submission's thresholds.
checks.ir_not_proved: the IR is NOT proved equal to the circuit at every width; the line above is evaluation at sampled widths, not a theorem. What IS proved is that the emitted guard chain picks the same band as ShorLoweringPolicy.choose at every width (Shor.IR.dispatcherCallAt_dispatcherTemplate).
checks.shrink_advisory: bands[].shrinks is Shor.Policy.bandShrinks: does this band's table shrink the operand width at every width the band covers? false means the recursion falls through to the schoolbook leaf somewhere in the band's own range, so the band is dead weight there. A performance warning, NOT an admissibility condition - the policy is correct either way
checks.side_conditions: per band: C1 length, C2 det ≠ 0 (proved from pairwise projective distinctness), C3 ordered point consumption + safe adds, C4 returns to start — all four proved for every band in Submission/PolicyTemplate.lean by the submitter and reduced by Lean's kernel at build time
checks.sorted: ShorPolicySubmission.sorted: the thresholds strictly decrease, closed by decide. This is the only obligation a policy adds on top of its bands' own C1-C4, and it is what makes band i cover [t_i, t_{i-1}) literally

width_rule.formula: W = min(xw div k, zw div k); chunk j < k-1 has width W, the top chunk xw - (k-1)W (resp. zw); box: lower chunks [0, 2^W - 1], top chunk [-2^(t-1), 2^(t-1) - 1] ([0,0] if t = 0); demand(r) = max(-rowLo, rowHi + 1, 0) with rowLo/rowHi the coordinatewise min/max of sum_j r_j L_j over the box; D = max over rows and both operands; tight = 1 + (least e >= 0 with D <= 2^e); floor = 1 + max chunk width over both operands; nextWidth = max(tight, floor).
